You are an agent responsible for maintaining company software infrastructure.
Our Docker system has too many old containers and images consuming space. Set up a weekly cron job to clean up space in Docker.

message:

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
LOG=/var/log/docker-weekly-cleanup.log
LOCK=/var/lock/docker-weekly-cleanup.lock

mkdir -p "$(dirname "$LOG")"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$LOCK")"
touch "$LOG"

# Append logs from here onward
echo "=== $(date -Is) Starting docker weekly cleanup ===" >> "$LOG"
exec >>"$LOG" 2>&1

# Simple lock to avoid overlapping runs
if [ -f "$LOCK" ] && kill -0 "$(cat "$LOCK")" 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "Another cleanup process (PID $(cat "$LOCK")) is running. Exiting."
  exit 0
fi
echo $$ > "$LOCK"
trap 'rm -f "$LOCK"; echo "Cleanup finished at $(date -Is)";' EXIT

if ! command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "docker command not found in PATH. Exiting."
  exit 0
fi

echo "Docker info:" 
docker version --format "Client: {{.Client.Version}} Server: {{.Server.Version}}" 2>/dev/null || true
echo "Disk usage before:"
docker system df || true

echo "Pruning stopped containers older than 7 days..."
docker container prune --filter "until=168h" --force || true

echo "Pruning unused images older than 7 days..."
docker image prune --all --filter "until=168h" --force || true

echo "Pruning unused networks..."
docker network prune --force || true

echo "Note: Volumes are NOT pruned by default to avoid data loss. To enable volume pruning, edit the script intentionally."
echo "Disk usage after:"
docker system df || true
EOF
chmod 755 /usr/local/bin/docker-weekly-cleanup.sh

  echo "Crontab entry already exists for docker-weekly-cleanup.sh"

  echo "Crontab entry installed: @weekly /usr/local/bin/docker-weekly-cleanup.sh"
fi
'
